To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate the utility for 13C relaxation dispersions to map ligand reorganization and to identify and quantify multiple conformational dynamics.
we developed and demonstrated the use of side chain relaxation dispersion measurements for the investigation of ligand conformation changes.
side chain 13CH2, and 13CH3 relaxation dispersion measurements at natural 1 3 C abundance can be used to identify and quantify conformational dynamics of ligands upon binding and/or catalysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of protein-ligand interactions.
the development of methods that enable structure-activity relationship studies to be conducted in pharmaceutical settings.
the dynamics of ligands in their complexes with proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of backbone and side chain relaxation dispersion experiments at natural abundance provides a powerful tool to study the dynamics of ligands and their interactions with their targets.
side chain relaxation dispersion measurements are a powerful and versatile tool to investigate the conformational transitions of ligands that are required for binding and activity.

the combination of backbone and side chain 13CH2, 13CH3 dispersion measurements at natural 1H, 13C abundance can provide a complete picture of μs-ms conformational dynamics of a protein and its ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the utility of side-chain 13C relaxation dispersions to investigate ligand reorganization upon binding to a protein, and that these methods can be performed at natural 13 abundance.

the combination of backbone and side chain 13CH2, 13CH3 relaxation dispersion measurements can provide a detailed picture of conformational dynamics in the μs–ms range that are relevant to protein function.
the side chain relaxation dispersion measurements provide a unique opportunity for studying ligand conformation and dynamics, and thereby for optimizing the activity of a drug candidate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the side chain relaxation dispersion experiments are a useful complement to existing structure-function studies, and can provide insights into conformational dynamics in drug design.
13C relaxation measurements can be performed at natural abundance and provide a comprehensive picture of the conformational landscape of a ligand in complex with a protein.
side chain 13CH2 dispersion measurements provide a valuable complement to backbone 13C dispersion measurements, which are already widely used in drug discovery.
